text:
alex_k: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on the mixed int4+fp8 path when serving long prefill (8k+ tokens). TTFT spikes ~2.8x and TPS drops under concurrent decode load.

maria: rough numbers? which model/config?

alex_k: model=rwkv-like-30b-quant, runtime=kern-v2, quant-profile=hybrid-int4-fp8, batcher=adaptive. Baseline (fp16) prefill 1.2s -> now 3.4s on same machine. Decode single-token latency similar but tail gets worse.

jin: can you attach a profile (nvprof/cupti or our perf traces)? sounds like kernel churn or repeated dequant/deq-copy.

alex_k: uploaded a short trace to /perf-traces/1950001234-flame.html and pasted the sampled stack:
```
kernel_dispatcher.cu: select_kernel(mha) -> swapped_kernel = fp8_prefill_kv
kv_cache.cu: merge_shards -> memcpy + quant_dequant_loop
quant.cu: dequantize_chunk (int4->fp16) x N
scheduler.cpp: microbatch_split -> fallback to smaller kernels
```

samuel: root cause might be the batching heuristic fallback we introduced last week — if prefill sees varied seq lengths it forces microbatching which triggers the int4 path more often. That amplifies per-token dequant overhead.

priya: do we see extra KV evictions? long contexts can push kv rotations and cause extra copies during prefill merge. Any logs for kv eviction/backpressure?

alex_k: yes — logs show repeated KV_EVICT and KV_MERGE entries right before the large prefill times. snippet: `KV_EVICT keys=1536 ratio=0.45; KV_MERGE shards=4 took=120ms`

maria: two quick experiments to try: 1) force prefill to use fp16 kernels (bypass int4 path) to confirm delta, 2) disable microbatch split for prefill-only workloads to measure TTFT/TPS tradeoff.

jin: +1. also try a short-lived hybrid calibration pass: run calibration for the long-prefix distribution (freq, token-id hist) and generate a per-layer scale table. int4/int8 quant quality can heavily affect whether we pick a vectorized kernel vs scalar decode.

perf-bot: Perf alert: /services/runtime/instance-7 saw p99 prefill latency increase from 1.4s -> 4.2s in the last deploy (rule: prefill-latency-regression). Link: https://perf.redwood/p/1950001234

alex_k: I ran experiment #1 (force fp16 kernels): prefill dropped to 1.3s, TPS improved ~2.6x. So kernel selection + quant dequant is main culprit.

samuel: ok that's strong signal. For a short-term patch: prefer decode-optimized kernels for long-prefill flows (heuristic: if prefill_tokens > 4096 and kv_shards>1, override quant kernel selection). Longer-term: add KV-aware dequant fusion to avoid roundtrip memcopies during kv merge.

priya: watch out for quality regressions if we bypass quant kernels. We should run eval suite (prompt set for long context) before rollout. I'll queue evals.

maria: I'll open a small PR for the heuristic override and include a feature flag + telemetry to measure TTFT/TPS and quality delta. Keep perf traces attached.

alex_k: thanks — attaching the minimal repro command: `redwoodctl bench --model rwkv-30b-q --prefill 8192 --concurrency 6 --quant hybrid-int4-fp8 --trace /tmp/trace1950001234`

jin: note: if we override kernel choice we should also disable microbatch splitting for prefill path to avoid extra scheduler overhead. That saved ~30% in my local run.

samuel: agree. PR should include a unit test that simulates varying seq lengths and asserts no microbatch split for prefill override.

perf-bot: CI perf regression check queued for PR #4421 (owner: maria).

alex_k: cool — I'll follow up with the KV memory maps and a proposed dequant fusion patch sketch. :thumbsup:
